title: Last Visited Integers
summary: Given an integer array nums, where each element is either a positive integer or -1.
statement: Given an integer array nums, where each element is either a positive integer or -1. For each -1 in the array, find the last visited positive integer. Initialize two empty arrays, seen and ans. Iterate through nums. If a positive integer is found, add it to the front of seen. If -1 is found, count the number of consecutive -1s. If this count is within the length of seen, append the corresponding element from seen to ans. Otherwise, append -1 to ans. Return the array ans.
constraints: Each element is either -1 or a positive integer.
A positive integer becomes the newest visited value and resets the consecutive -1 counter.
The first -1 returns the newest positive value, the second consecutive -1 the second-newest, and so on; return -1 when unavailable.
hints: Store integer visits in their original order.
Track how many prev commands have occurred since the last integer.
For a query, use that count as a one-based offset from the end; reset it when an integer arrives.
The list is the complete visit history and the offset exactly encodes which most-recent entry the current query requests.
editorial: The list is the complete visit history and the offset exactly encodes which most-recent entry the current query requests.

tests.explanation: The three queries request the newest, second-newest, and a missing third value.
Reading 2 resets the offset before the final two queries.
